output:
Short answer
- Start with the Meadowlight Lamp — your catalog/memory shows it as the recommended, “independently certified for exceptional energy efficiency” option for sustainable office upgrades. Treat that as a candidate to evaluate, not a final purchase decision.

Why I recommend considering Meadowlight
- Catalog evidence in memory: multiple catalog entries describe the Meadowlight Lamp as a standard office desk lamp, “independently certified for exceptional energy efficiency,” and recommended for sustainable office upgrades.
- That makes it a good first candidate because procurement teams typically start with catalog-recommended, certified products.

What still needs verification (these claims require proof)
- “Independently certified for exceptional energy efficiency” — verify which certification body (ENERGY STAR, DLC, EU ecolabel, etc.), and get the certification number or listing.
- Actual energy performance — confirm measured lumens, wattage and efficacy (lm/W) from LM-79 lab test results or the official spec sheet.
- Lifetime and degradation — request LM-80 or equivalent LED lumen maintenance data and rated lifetime (hours).
- Photometric performance — confirm lumen output, CCT (color temperature), CRI, and flicker data to ensure good task lighting quality.
- Adjustability and ergonomics — confirm head/arm articulation, range, and user controls (dimming, presets) against your office needs.
- Warranty, service, and availability — verify warranty length, replacement parts (LED module replaceability), and lead time/pricing.
- Any sustainability claims beyond energy efficiency (e.g., recycled materials, take-back) — ask for supporting documentation.

Minimum spec targets to use when comparing options
- Efficacy: >= 80–120 lm/W (better is >100 lm/W for very efficient fixtures)
- Lumen output: choose based on task — typical desk task lights: 300–1,000 lumens directed at task
- CRI: >= 80 for general office, >= 90 if color-critical work
- CCT: 3000–4000 K (3500 K common for mixed offices)
- Dimmable: yes (and compatible with common controls)
- Flicker: low (ask for percent flicker or strobe index)
- Rated life: >= 35,000–50,000 hours; provide LM-80 data
- Certification: ENERGY STAR and/or DLC listing preferred

Procurement verification checklist (what to request from vendor)
1. Product spec sheet (lumens, wattage, lm/W, CCT, CRI, dimming type).  
2. LM-79 photometric test report (measured lumens and efficacy).  
3. LM-80 lumen maintenance data and rated life estimate + TM-21 extrapolation.  
4. Certification listing (ENERGY STAR/DLC/etc.) with listing number or link.  
5. Warranty terms and service/repair policy.  
6. Photometric files (IES/IESNA) if you will model lighting levels.  
7. Price, lead time, and bulk-purchase discounts.  
8. Sample unit for workplace trial (highly recommended).

If you want alternatives
- Look for desk/task lamps that explicitly list ENERGY STAR or DLC certification and meet the spec targets above. If you’d like, I can search available catalog / marketplace options and list 3–5 ENERGY STAR/DLC-certified desk lamps to compare.

Next steps I can do for you
- Draft a short vendor email requesting the verification documents above for the Meadowlight Lamp.  
- Compare Meadowlight’s spec sheet (if you upload it) against the checklist and give a go/no-go recommendation.  
- Search for and shortlist other ENERGY STAR/DLC-certified desk lamps if you want alternatives.

Which of those would you like me to do next?
